attacker_start: Authenticated user able to initiate a group bulk import in the historical GitLab deployment.
attacker_control: The upload archive supplied by the import source, including a symbolic-link entry and its link target.
primitive: An archive symlink survives extraction and is later followed as a local file.
boundary: Untrusted imported archive content crosses into the GitLab server's local filesystem read authority.
enforcing_component: UploadsPipeline extract/load path, including untar_zxf, file-path enumeration, and File.open.
sink: UploadService copies the opened file content into a group upload that the importing user can read.
capability_delta: The importer can obtain server-local files readable by the GitLab process, beyond files contained in the source archive.
prerequisites: A group import permitted to the attacker and an import source/archive the attacker can control; local file permissions still limit readable targets.
proof_oracle: The public historical report shows an imported upload returning content from a server-local file. This card records the report's evidence; it is not a fresh reproduction.
root_cause: The extraction path did not reject the symlink, and the later File.open consumed its resolved target without enforcing containment within the extracted archive tree.
chain_edges: Attacker-controlled archive member -> retained symlink in extracted uploads
Retained symlink -> server-local file read by File.open
Server-local file read -> content stored and served through the import upload
patch_or_fix: The historical issue identifies the UploadsPipeline link/containment boundary. GitLab's later merge request !107161 describes additional path checks as defense in depth; it is not asserted here to be the original fix.
duplicate_signature: GitLab group bulk import UploadsPipeline | symlink in uploaded tar archive | no link-target containment before File.open | UploadService with server-local read authority | imported upload exposes local file content
analyst_notes: Historical, publicly disclosed root only. The issue mirrors the researcher report and includes source snippets and observed upload read-back. No independently executed reproduction or original fixing commit was verified. The later MR explicitly calls its changes defense in depth. Do not infer current-release vulnerability from this card.

attacker_start: A user able to start a GitHub repository import in the historical GitLab 15.3.1-ee test environment.
attacker_control: A GitHub-compatible API response consumed by the importer, including a non-scalar default_branch value with keys that become Ruby methods.
entry_point: GitLab GitHub importer's repository metadata processing and default-branch update.
primitive: Sawyer::Resource turns attacker-controlled JSON keys into methods, allowing inconsistent to_s and bytesize behavior at Redis command serialization.
boundary: Untrusted upstream API JSON crosses into trusted Ruby object behavior, then Redis protocol framing and session-state consumption.
enforcing_component: Gitlab::GithubImport::Importer::RepositoryImporter, repository branch cache, and Redis command helper.
sink: Redis command stream; the historical report further chains injected session state into Marshal deserialization.
capability_delta: The historical test demonstrated attacker-influenced Redis commands and reported command execution through a session-deserialization chain.
prerequisites: A permitted GitHub import, a GitHub API response source under attacker control in the tested configuration, vulnerable Sawyer/Redis behavior, and a reachable session-deserialization consumer for the terminal effect.
proof_oracle: The public report includes historical Redis traffic and a GitLab 15.3.1-ee test trace for the chain. This card does not claim an independent reproduction or current production reachability.
root_cause: The importer passed a dynamic Sawyer::Resource value as a branch identifier to a Redis-backed branch cache without normalizing it to a trusted scalar. Redis length calculation and emitted value could then disagree, permitting protocol-command injection.
chain_edges: Attacker-controlled API JSON -> dynamic Sawyer::Resource method behavior
Dynamic branch value -> Redis protocol framing discrepancy and command injection
Injected Redis session state -> historical Marshal-deserialization command-execution chain
patch_or_fix: Normalize Octokit/Sawyer responses before authority-bearing consumers and prevent dynamic methods from overriding Ruby behavior. GitLab MR !98231 describes the latter hardening, but is not asserted to be the exact initial fix for this report.
duplicate_signature: GitLab GitHub import RepositoryImporter | API JSON default_branch represented as Sawyer::Resource | no scalar normalization before Redis cache | Redis serializer and session consumer | Redis command injection with historical command-execution chain
analyst_notes: Historical, publicly disclosed root only. The public issue states that GitLab 15.3.1-ee was affected in the researcher's test. The Hacktivity-generated summary instead claims it was patched in 15.3.1-ee; that patch-version claim is contradicted by the primary report and must not be propagated. The exact first fixing release and current-release state were not independently verified. No executable payloads are stored in this card.

attacker_start: Authenticated GitLab user authorized to import projects, in a historical deployment with the bulk_import_projects and size-validation paths enabled.
attacker_control: Imported project attributes, including an import_source value that reaches an archive path after incomplete attribute filtering.
entry_point: BulkImports::Projects::Pipelines::ProjectPipeline creates an imported project whose archive is processed by Gitlab::ImportExport::FileImporter.
primitive: An attacker-controlled archive path is interpolated into a shell command string passed to Open3.popen3.
boundary: Untrusted project-import metadata crosses into server-side command interpretation under the GitLab worker's authority.
sink: Open3.popen3 executes the archive-size command constructed with the import_source-derived path.
capability_delta: In the historical vulnerable configuration, the importing user can execute commands as the GitLab import worker.
prerequisites: Project-import authority; the relevant bulk-import feature and archive-size validation path enabled; crafted import metadata accepted by the pipeline. The report says bulk project imports were disabled by default for self-managed installations and scoped on GitLab.com at the time.
proof_oracle: The maintainer-mirrored report includes a historical GitLab 15.1.0-ee local test and worker output showing the controlled command effect. This card is not an independent reproduction.
root_cause: ProjectPipeline failed to remove the import_source attribute before project creation, and DecompressedArchiveSizeValidator embedded the resulting archive path into a shell-interpreted string instead of passing separated arguments.
patch_or_fix: GitLab's CVE-2022-2185 record lists fixed branches at 14.10.5, 15.0.4, and 15.1.1. The report identifies attribute allowlisting and argument-array command execution as the relevant fix loci; exact commit-level lineage was not checked here.
duplicate_signature: GitLab Project BulkImports and DecompressedArchiveSizeValidator | import_source attribute in untrusted project metadata | incomplete attribute filter plus shell-interpreted archive-path interpolation | Open3.popen3 in import worker | historical command execution
analyst_notes: Historical, publicly disclosed root only. The public issue explicitly records the feature-flag and deployment caveat; do not generalize the local 15.1.0-ee proof to default self-managed or current GitLab.com exposure. The CVE gives historical fixed version ranges, not proof about today's release. No executable payloads are stored in this card.
